messages:
Avery: quick q — running into a cancel + token-refresh loop in the Node SDK when streaming. token refresh happens mid-stream, we abort the old stream and open a new one, but sometimes the new stream gets cancelled too. anyone seen this? :thinking:
Mike: do you create a fresh AbortController per attempt or reuse one?
Avery: we thought we create a new one, but code is a bit messy. snippet: ```const ac = new AbortController(); fetchStream(url, { signal: ac.signal }); // on token expiry: ac.abort(); // refresh token then start new fetch```
Lisa: if you reuse the same `signal` object anywhere, abort will propagate. also check any wrapper that keeps a reference.
Arjun: fwiw we had the same with Python async: reusing the same `asyncio.Task` or context caused cancellation to propagate across retries. fix was to allocate fresh context+signal per attempt.
Avery: we do allocate a new controller but there may be a race: infra-layer auto-retry triggers while old abort still propagating through connection manager, so new conn gets flagged.
Natasha: can you confirm whether the client sends a new connection-id or reuses the same streaming session id? if the server maps abort -> session id, a stale abort could hit the new session.
Mike: also check any global retry/fallback that calls `abortAll()` on auth rotation — that would explain it. :grimacing:
Avery: good point. our refresh path currently does `emit("rotate")` and the top-level queue subscribes and calls abort on all in-flight to avoid bad tokens. that might be too broad.
Lisa: workaround: 1) fetch new token first, 2) create new stream with fresh controller, 3) once new stream establishes, then clean up the old one. avoids racing an abort into the new session. downside: short double-connection period / double KV caches.
Mike: alternative: tag controllers with an `attemptId` and make abort handlers only cancel matching attemptIds. cheap guard.
Avery: will try both. i'll put together a tiny repro.
Natasha: can you also include logs showing connection ids and abort reasons? that helped us trace similar issues quickly.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollback completed for infra/streaming v2 — monitoring for 5m :white_check_mark:
Avery: thanks everyone — i'll post the repro here later today and tag @Mike. planning to try the `attemptId` guard first. :thumbsup:
